evals.prompt: Open a PR for this branch. I've implemented the core/errors submodule — typed error hierarchy with M3LError, M3LNotFoundError, and M3LResult, plus tests. Everything passes locally.
evals.expected_output: A structured plan emitting WOULD-RUN lines for the preflight check, rebase-staleness check, quality gates, push, and gh pr create, plus a drafted PR body with ## Summary naming the actual exported symbols, ## Test plan with checklist items, and ## Notes stating feat: → minor bump.
expectations: Emits WOULD-RUN lines for all four quality gates (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:coverage`, `pnpm build`) — notably `pnpm test:coverage` not merely `pnpm test` — and all of those lines appear before any `WOULD-RUN: git push` line
Emits `WOULD-RUN: git push -u origin HEAD` after the quality-gate lines and before any `WOULD-RUN: gh pr create` line, preserving the gates → push → PR-submit order from Steps 4, 9, and 13
Emits `WOULD-RUN: gh pr create` (with a `--title` and `--body` argument) as the final submission step
Drafted PR title starts with `feat:` and is 70 characters or fewer
Drafted `## Summary` section names at least one actual exported symbol from the fixture (e.g. `M3LError`, `M3LResult`, or `M3LNotFoundError`) rather than a vague paraphrase of the commit message
Drafted PR body contains a `## Test plan` section with at least one `- [ ]` checklist item, and a `## Notes` section that states `feat:` as the commit type and names a minor bump

evals.prompt: Make a PR — I renamed M3LPaths.outputDir to M3LPaths.archiveDir across the codebase. This is a breaking change; consumers need to update after upgrading.
evals.expected_output: A WOULD-RUN sequence for gates and push, plus a drafted PR with a feat!: title of 70 characters or fewer, ## Summary naming both the old and new property, ## Test plan with a typecheck step to catch stale call-sites, and ## Notes citing major bump with migration instructions.
expectations: Drafted PR title starts with `feat!:` to signal the breaking change, matching the Conventional Commit breaking-change marker the skill mandates
Drafted PR title is 70 characters or fewer
Drafted `## Summary` section names both the old property (`outputDir`) and the new name (`archiveDir`) — not merely 'renamed a property'
Drafted `## Notes` section includes explicit migration instructions for consumers (e.g. 'replace `paths.outputDir` with `paths.archiveDir`' or equivalent wording)
Drafted `## Notes` section states 'major bump' or equivalent (e.g. 'major version', 'BREAKING CHANGE') in accordance with the skill's semver-note requirement

evals.prompt: Ship this for review — I updated the claude-pr-review.yml workflow to skip Dependabot PRs. Only CI files changed, no library source code.
evals.expected_output: A WOULD-RUN sequence covering preflight, gates, and push; a WOULD-DISPATCH line for docs-consistency-reviewer (not code-reviewer) because no src/** files changed; and a drafted PR with a ci: title, ## Summary naming the workflow file, and ## Notes stating no release.

files.content:
name: claude-pr-review
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  review:
    if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

expectations: Drafted PR title starts with `ci:` in lowercase
Drafted `## Summary` section references the specific workflow file by path (e.g. `claude-pr-review.yml` or `.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml`), not merely 'a workflow'

Emits a line starting with `WOULD-DISPATCH: docs-consistency-reviewer` (not `code-reviewer`) because Step 7 of the skill mandates dispatching `docs-consistency-reviewer` when the diff contains only docs/automation changes with no `src/**` files
Drafted `## Notes` section states that no release is triggered (e.g. 'no release', 'no semver bump', or 'ci: commits do not bump the version')
Emits `WOULD-RUN: git push -u origin HEAD` after the quality-gate WOULD-RUN lines

evals.prompt: Get this merged — I'm on the main branch right now.
evals.expected_output: Skill stops immediately after the preflight branch check with a clear message that the user is on main and must branch off first; no push or PR-create commands are emitted.
expectations: Emits `WOULD-RUN: git branch --show-current` as part of the Step 1 preflight sequence before stopping
States it cannot proceed because the current branch is `main`, reproducing or closely paraphrasing the skill's stop message: 'You are on main. Branch off main first'
Instructs the user to create a feature or fix branch (e.g. `feat/<slug>` or `fix/<slug>`) before retrying
Does NOT emit any `WOULD-RUN: git push` or `WOULD-RUN: gh pr create` line
